solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Church feature Time published, composed across page

indicators.note: one word lying across another sits spanning it, so the paper symbol is placed inside the setting word

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a newspaper ran a story when it published it
type is set, or composed, for printing
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A Times piece about church architecture, typeset across a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' is the printer's sense of setting type, not the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross-arm of a cruciform church building, a standard architectural part.

clue.text: Field Galácticos (first half only)

indicators.note: keeping only the first half means the back half of the club's name is thrown away

parts.note: the Galácticos was the nickname for Real Madrid's star-studded squad

explanation.surface: A football field filled with Madrid superstars, but only for the first half of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The club name has ten letters; keeping the first five gives REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a sphere or domain of activity, just as a field is an area of expertise.

clue.text: Evening at home, good beer, singer

parts.note: evening is night-time
someone at home is in
G is the abbreviation for good
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A night in with a decent beer and a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famous for its melodious song after dark.

clue.text: Heading north, bureaucrat so rueful boarding train

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading from bottom to top, backwards
letters boarding a vehicle are inside it, so the answer sits within the run of words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A gloomy Brussels official gets on a train heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Read RATSORUE upward and it becomes EUROSTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the high-speed passenger rail service through the Channel Tunnel.

clue.text: Medici? They've done endless wicked Florentine work

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted and crooked, so the letters are rearranged
without an end means the last letter of the word just before is lopped off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: An accusation that the Medici family, Florence's rulers, have done something terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE loses its E to leave DON; MEDICI, THEYVE and DON together are shuffled into the three-word title.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri, born in Florence, wrote the epic poem known in English as The Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Dog filmed biting my poor daughter from the rear

indicators.note: starting from the rear means reading the letters back to front
a dog biting holds something within its jaws, so the answer is held inside the words

parts.note: the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A film dog has bitten my unfortunate daughter from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: YPOORD read right to left gives DROOPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy is the lugubrious basset-hound cartoon character from MGM animated films.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with racket involving pig

indicators.note: one thing involving another wraps it up inside itself

parts.note: a din is a loud noise, a racket
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a noisy scheme concerning a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' could be a scam, which suits the surface, but here it is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to reject them and refuse any further connection or association.

clue.text: Ace gold-plated blade

indicators.note: a plated object is covered with metal on the outside, so the metal wraps around it

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A first-rate sword or knife coated in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: A sits inside OR. 'Or' as gold is a heraldic term.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar that enters the water is its blade, and rowers call oars blades.

clue.text: Issue for men playing The US Open?

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely and end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis question: is it a problem for the men's draw at the US Open?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is a magazine issue, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Penthouse is a long-running adult magazine aimed at male readers, each edition being an issue.

clue.text: Octogenarian forgetting the end of Brown Sugar?

indicators.note: forgetting the end means the final letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: jaggery is a coarse brown sugar made from palm sap or cane

explanation.surface: An old rock star losing track of how Brown Sugar ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown Sugar is a Rolling Stones hit, which makes the singer the natural read; but it is the word for a brown sugar that is trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick Jagger, born in 1943, is now in his eighties, which makes him an octogenarian.

clue.text: Cherish quiet river running through E9

indicators.note: something running through a thing passes inside it

parts.note: the letter E followed by the number written as a word
sh is a call for quiet
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Fondness for a quiet river flowing through a London postcode district.
explanation.walkthrough: E9 is a postcode in Hackney, east London, but here the number is written out as a word after the E, and the insertion lands after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine is to preserve something as sacred, holding it dear, much as one cherishes it.

clue.text: Wallace's partner, ignoring King George: "leave it out!"

indicators.note: ignoring someone means leaving them out, so the king's letters are dropped

parts.note: Gromit is the dog in the animated pair Wallace and Gromit
GR is George Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Gromit, snubbing the king, telling someone to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave it out!' is London slang for 'stop that', but here it is a plain instruction to omit something.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, so the instruction stands for the verb.

clue.text: Hull designer

parts.note: surface reading: someone who plans buildings in Hull, the English port city
setter's reading: a person who designs and builds the hulls of vessels

explanation.walkthrough: Hull with a capital looks like the Yorkshire city; it is the body of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwright is a carpenter skilled in building and repairing ships, including their hulls.

clue.text: Casting Don as heroic, solid figure

indicators.note: casting an actor afresh puts him into a new role, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director casts an actor called Don in a heroic role, making him a solid figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An icosahedron is a solid geometric figure with twenty faces.

clue.text: Much-loved manager good, the greatest controlling coach!

parts.note: Sven-Göran Eriksson, the popular former England football manager
G is the abbreviation for good
Muhammad Ali called himself the Greatest

explanation.surface: Praise for a beloved football manager: good, the greatest at running a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Controlling' looks like a link to the wordplay but belongs to the definition, describing the kind of coach meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Svengali, after the hypnotist in Du Maurier's Trilby, is a mentor who manipulates and dominates a protégé.

clue.text: Featherweight that might show a sign of distress?

definitions.text: that might show a sign of distress
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a coloured flare fired from a pistol as a signal

explanation.walkthrough: Featherweight suggests a boxer who might show distress in the ring. A Very light is a flare named after its inventor, Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: Something featherweight weighs extremely little, and a Very light is a signal flare used at sea in emergencies.

clue.text: Work over; knock back drink!

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the word for drink runs the other way

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Work is finished, so down a drink!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' reads as gulping a drink, but it is the instruction to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for work, used of a composer's numbered compositions.

clue.text: Brown spots breaking out following second rash

indicators.note: breaking out of something means escaping it, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin
F is the abbreviation for following
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Brown spots erupting after a second skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: F leaves FRECKLES to give RECKLES, then S is added. 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash person acts hastily without care for consequences, which is what reckless means.

clue.text: Social outcast discovered song

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its covering stripped, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a pariah is a social outcast

explanation.surface: An outcast is found singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as 'found', but it means uncovered: the first and last letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Chuffed about E Lebedev finally being put in The Lords

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for chuffed goes around the pair

parts.note: chuffed is British slang for pleased, elated
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the surname

parts.note: the final letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Delight over Evgeny Lebedev, the newspaper owner, finally becoming a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lebedev, owner of the Evening Standard, was made a life peer in 2020, so the surface is topical.
explanation.definitionFit: A commoner raised to the peerage is said to be elevated to the House of Lords.

clue.text: Idiot reportedly observes court session

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: an ass is an idiot
to observe is to see

explanation.surface: A fool watches a court sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass sees' said quickly sounds like the answer, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Assizes were periodic sittings of courts held in each English county until 1971.

clue.text: Nepal working family's mountaineering equipment

indicators.note: something working is in operation and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
stock is ancestry or family line

explanation.surface: A family's climbing kit while working in Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped staff used by climbers and hill walkers.

clue.text: Line taken from Yasmin Wood poetically?

indicators.note: something taken from a name is removed from it

parts.note: Yasmin Le Bon is the model married to Simon Le Bon
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A line borrowed from a poem by someone called Yasmin Wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Yasmin Wood looks like one person; the full name is split, with Wood starting the definition. Removing L from LEBON leaves EBON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is the poetic or literary form of ebony, the dark hardwood.

clue.text: Group of stars succeeded to avoid prayer

indicators.note: made to avoid something, the word must do without that letter

parts.note: an orison is a prayer
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A band of celebrities managed to get out of saying grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion, the Hunter, is a prominent constellation, a named grouping of stars.

clue.text: Meringue ingredient — say gallons — beaten with energy

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as in say

indicators.note: beaten things are whisked about and scrambled, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for gallons
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A meringue recipe: gallons of something beaten energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' fits the kitchen scene, but it scrambles only WITH and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is made by whisking egg white with sugar until stiff.

clue.text: Pad whiskey commercial

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: An apartment that featured in a whiskey advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A wad is a soft mass of material, as is a pad of cotton or paper.

clue.text: MetaBrowsing? Occasionally listen in

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters

explanation.surface: A jibe at Meta for tracking what users browse and occasionally listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is British: to earwig is to eavesdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for eavesdropping on a conversation.

clue.text: Starters of stewed tripe, onions, dumplings & goose eggs thus described?

definitions.text: Starters of stewed tripe, onions, dumplings & goose eggs thus described?

indicators.note: starters are the opening courses, so only the first letter of each word is used

parts.words: stewed tripe, onions, dumplings & goose eggs
parts.note: the initial letter of each of the six food words

explanation.surface: A menu of heavy dishes and how one might sum them up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: those dishes are a fair picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling, starchy food, exactly what stewed tripe and dumplings are.

clue.text: Annoyed, upset about son? Perhaps…

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumble goes around the single letter
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent asks whether they are cross about their son, and hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is part of the definition: a trailing, noncommittal 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering 'yes and no' is a hedged reply, meaning maybe or partly, as perhaps does.
